en: Contrary to the misconception that Magellan discovered the Philippines, indigenous communities already inhabited the islands thousands of years before his 1521 arrival.
Unlike the common belief that Jose Rizal was the first president, Emilio Aguinaldo actually held the presidential office first in 1899.
Contrary to the belief that July 4 is Independence Day, the Philippines actually declared independence from Spain on June 12, 1898.
Despite the misconception that the Philippine eagle only eats monkeys, it primarily hunts flying foxes, civets, and snakes in the wild.
Unlike the misconception that Filipino is purely Tagalog, the national language actually incorporates words from other regional languages like Cebuano and Ilocano.
Contrary to the belief that the flag's eight sun rays represent regions, they actually symbolize the first eight provinces that revolted against Spain.
Unlike the misconception that Fe del Mundo was the first Filipina doctor, Honoria Acosta actually earned the first medical degree in 1909.
Contrary to the belief that the Barong Tagalog is made of thick cloth, it uses delicate, translucent piña fabric to keep wearers cool.
Unlike the misconception that the Senate and House have the same size, the Senate has exactly 24 members while the House has over 300.
Contrary to the myth of a fair duel, Lapu-Lapu's forces overwhelmed and killed Magellan with a group of native warriors at Mactan.
Unlike the misconception that the Philippine tarsier is blind, it actually uses its large, forward-facing eyes to hunt insects at night.
Contrary to the belief that the Ibong Adarna is a real bird, it is actually a mythical creature from a famous Filipino epic.
